study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier (e.g., AuthorX_YYYY) is given in the text.

subject_id.notes: Paper reports aggregate cohort statistics only; no per-subject IDs are provided in the main or supplementary text extracted.

sample_id.notes: No per-sample identifiers reported in provided text.

pmid.notes: paper_id (37069399) supplied externally resembles a PMID but is not stated within the paper text itself.

subcohort.notes: AN-RS and AN-BP subtypes are mentioned as diagnostic subtypes but not framed as a formal 'subcohort' field.

target_condition.evidence_quote: The gut microbiota contributes to the pathogenesis of anorexia nervosa in humans and mice

control.evidence_quote: a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
control.notes: 77 AN cases labeled as Case; 70 healthy controls (HC) labeled as Study Control.

country.evidence_quote: recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark from 1 September 12014 to 31 July 2016

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
body_site.notes: Serum samples were also collected for metabolomics but body_site enum best matches feces for the gut microbiome samples.

days_from_first_collection.notes: Study is cross-sectional; no repeated collection time points reported for human samples.

location.evidence_quote: Center for Eating Disorders (Odense University Hospital), Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital) and Unit for Psychiatric Research (Aalborg University Hospital)

westernized.notes: Cohort is Danish, implying westernized lifestyle, but not explicitly stated.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Same 3-month antibiotic exclusion also applied to healthy controls.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Protocol name given (IHMS SOP P7 V2) but no specific commercial kit matching allowed enum values reported for human samples; mouse samples used NucleoSpin soil mini kit (not in allowed list).

ncbi_accession.notes: No accession number found in provided text.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: Human faecal shotgun metagenomics used Ion Proton; mouse 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (donor stools/recipient caecal content) used Illumina MiSeq, a different platform for a different sample type.

age.notes: Detailed age values reported in Supplementary Table 1/2, not included in provided text.

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

sex.evidence_quote: we decided to include only women in the present study
sex.notes: Both AN cases and age-matched HC women were exclusively female.

zigosity.notes: Not a twin study; zygosity not applicable/reported.

age_min.notes: Only 'age-matched' description given for the main cohort; exact aggregate age range not reported in provided text (referenced Supplementary Table 1/2 not included).

age_max.notes: Same as age_min; aggregate value not available in provided text.

age_years.notes: Aggregate mean age for the 77 AN / 70 HC cohort not given in main text; only individual donor ages reported (see samples).

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion refers to antibiotic use within previous 3 months, implying no current antibiotic use for all enrolled participants (AN and HC).

bmi.evidence_quote: women with AN were much leaner
bmi.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
bmi.notes: Only qualitative leanness statement given for the aggregate cohort; specific numeric BMI values for the full cohort are in Supplementary Tables 1/2, not provided in text. Specific numeric BMI values ARE given for the 6 FMT donor individuals (see samples).

dietary_restriction.notes: No formal dietary restriction category (e.g., vegetarian/gluten-free) reported for human participants; energy-restricted diet applies to mice, not humans.

disease.evidence_quote: a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females

disease_details.evidence_quote: the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples were collected but no specific stool phenotype term (e.g., diarrhea) was reported.

fmt_id.notes: Donors described only as 'three patients with AN' and 'three HC' without individual IDs.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: we transplanted faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain
fmt_role.notes: Applies to the six human FMT donor participants; mouse recipients are not human samples for this schema.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Exclusion criteria for controls allowed birth control pill use, but individual usage status not confirmed for any participant.

smoker.evidence_quote: confounders including age, smoking and multiple drug intake
smoker.section: Results — Associations between absolute bacterial abundance and bioclinical variables
smoker.notes: Smoking used as a statistical covariate; actual smoker/non-smoker counts or status not reported in provided text.

treatment.evidence_quote: medications (selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines, specified in Supplementary Table 2)
treatment.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
treatment.notes: These medications were used as deconfounding covariates for a subset of AN cases; not all AN participants were on these medications.

biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers such as glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR and CRP are mentioned qualitatively (e.g., 'lower fasting serum concentrations of glucose and insulin') but exact numeric values are reported only in Supplementary Tables 1-2, which were not included in the provided text.

biomarker_unit.notes: No explicit unit values found in accessible main text for biomarkers; values reside in unprovided Supplementary Tables.

biomarker_value.notes: Quantitative biomarker values (glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, CRP) are referenced qualitatively only; exact figures are in Supplementary Table 1/2 not included in the provided text.

disease_response_os.notes: This is not an oncology/survival study; overall survival is not applicable to this AN gut microbiota paper.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no overall survival data reported.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is an oncology-specific measure not used in this eating-disorder study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No field named 'feces_phenotype' or corresponding values explicitly reported; the paper reports fecal microbiota composition data (species, diversity indices) but not a defined 'feces_phenotype' variable.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor-related measurements in this study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor resection or residual tumor data in this study.

extraction_warnings: Paper reports only aggregate/group-level statistics (AN vs HC, and AN-RS vs AN-BP subtypes); no per-subject or per-sample data table was found in the provided text, so sample_level extraction was not possible.

Granularity was set to subgroup_level (AN vs HC) primarily because case/control status differs between groups; most demographic/clinical detail fields (age, BMI, etc.) are stated to be in Supplementary Tables 1-2, which were not included in the provided text.
study_name, subject_id, sample_id, ncbi_accession, and dna_extraction_kit could not be populated due to absence of this information in the provided text.

Mouse experiments used a different sequencing platform (Illumina MiSeq for 16S rRNA) than human samples (Ion Proton for shotgun metagenomics); only the human platform was recorded as the primary sequencing_platform value.
pmid was left not_reported because the paper text itself does not state its own PubMed ID; the provided paper_id (37069399) appears to be the PMID but this is external metadata, not extracted text.
Batch 1 returned granularity='sample_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['AN', 'HC']; kept batch 0.

Aggregate demographic/clinical data for the full 77 AN / 70 HC cohort (age, BMI, medication use, smoking status) are referenced as Supplementary Tables 1 and 2, but the actual table contents were not included in the provided text, limiting study-level numeric extraction.

Sample-level rows were extracted only for the 6 individually described FMT donor participants (3 AN, 3 HC); the remaining 141 participants are only described in aggregate terms not fully detailed in the provided text.
Smoking and medication use are mentioned only as statistical covariates without reported per-group frequencies/values in the main text.
Antibiotic use inference is based on an exclusion criterion (no antibiotics within previous 3 months), not a direct statement of current use status.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['AN', 'HC']; kept batch 0.
Most schema fields (biomarker values, ECOG, OS, tumor size) pertain to oncology-style studies and are not applicable to this gut microbiota/anorexia nervosa paper; marked as not_reported.

Specific numeric biomarker values (glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, CRP, etc.) are referenced qualitatively in the main text but the actual numeric data reside in Supplementary Tables 1-2, which were not provided in the input.
host_species field required a single string but the study involves both human participants and mouse models (FMT experiments); both were noted for completeness.
feces_phenotype_value field has no directly corresponding defined variable in the paper; fecal microbiota composition metrics were reported instead but not under this exact field name.
